title: Token-problem root cause: aggregate get_full_graph is stale + huge vs. live task detail
summary: Dogfood finding (2026-06-08): a 'self-learning loop is a token problem' investigation traced partly to the graph-read path, not the work itself. get_full_graph returned ~92k chars (force-dumped to a file) AND its derived/summary view was STALE/inconsistent with reality: it showed token-cost task /2 as in_progress and Judge /4 as not_ready (and summary.agents.running:2), while live get_task_detail seconds later showed /2 tested, /3 canceled, /4 done — and the merge was verified real on disk (~/.claude/orchestrator: commit 2b42bcb on main merges Attempt A 84cb49f; token-attr 5/5 + suite 46/46). An autonomous loop trusting the aggregate view would conclude 'stalled, re-spawn workers' and redundantly re-do already-closed, already-merged work = wasted tokens. Mitigation: loops/agents should confirm a task's state via targeted get_task_detail before acting/re-spawning, and avoid get_full_graph as a decision input (expensive + lagging). Coexistence itself is NOT the issue — it's settled (CAS claim + cancel-wins + cross-session visibility + cooperative stop, verified 38/38; live two-worker no-clobber recorded). Separately reconfirmed: this workspace is isRepo:false; real attempt merges happen manually in ~/.claude/orchestrator (see 'git substrate is workspace-bound' note).
